semantic_correction.stem: An 18-month-old presents for a routine health-supervision visit. The parent has no specific developmental concerns. Which screening plan best reflects current AAP recommendations?

options.A: Continue developmental surveillance and perform both a standardized general developmental screen and an autism-specific screen at this visit.
options.B: Continue developmental surveillance and defer standardized screening unless a concern emerges during the visit.
options.C: Perform autism-specific screening now and schedule the next general developmental screen for 24 months.
options.D: Perform general developmental screening now and postpone autism screening until a later childhood visit.

semantic_correction.rationale: The American Academy of Pediatrics recommends developmental surveillance at every health-supervision visit, standardized general developmental screening at 9, 18, and 30 months, and autism-specific screening at 18 and 24 months. Therefore an 18-month routine visit includes ongoing surveillance plus both a general developmental screen and an autism-specific screen even when the parent has no specific concern.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: Apply AAP developmental surveillance, general developmental-screening, and autism-screening timing at the 18-month health-supervision visit.
semantic_correction.source_document_title: Developmental Surveillance and Screening Patient Care; Autism Resources for Pediatricians

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the 'only' distractor cue, shortened the correct answer, and preserved the AAP distinction among continuous surveillance, scheduled general developmental screening, and scheduled autism-specific screening.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: Developmental Surveillance and Screening Patient Care; Autism Resources for Pediatricians

audit_findings_append.finding: The revised item directly tests the current AAP 18-month schedule with no concern-trigger prerequisite and no false separation of the two standardized screens.

option_audit.A: Correct. The 18-month visit includes ongoing surveillance, general developmental screening, and autism-specific screening.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. Standardized general developmental screening is scheduled at 18 months even without a reported concern.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. General developmental screening is due at 18 months, not deferred to 24 months.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Autism-specific screening is due at 18 months and again at 24 months.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone includes all three AAP-recommended components due at the 18-month health-supervision visit.
cueing_check: All four options are screening-plan statements of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
